title: Globalizing ordinary point-blowup towers from finitely many local schemes
statement: Let $S$ be an integral normal Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; Noetherian here means that $S$ has a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Let $s_1,\ldots,s_r$ be distinct closed points, where $r\geq0$, put $U=S\setminus\{s_1,\ldots,s_r\}$, and set $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s_i}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every $i$, give a finite tower $T_{i,n_i}\to\cdots\to T_{i,0}=S_i$ of ordinary blowups at reduced closed points lying over $s_i$ [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Assume every $T_{i,j}$ is integral and normal. There is a tower $Z_N\to\cdots\to Z_0=S$, with $N=\sum_i n_i$, of ordinary blowups at reduced closed points over $\{s_1,\ldots,s_r\}$. Every $Z_j$ is integral, normal and Noetherian; every arrow is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and is an isomorphism away from its center. The base change of this tower to $S_i$ is the prescribed tower after insertion of identity arrows [def-pc-fibre-product]. More precisely there are integers $a_i(j)$ with $a_i(0)=0$ and $a_i(N)=n_i$; at each global step exactly one $a_i$ increases by one, and $Z_j\times_S S_i\cong T_{i,a_i(j)}$ compatibly with the arrows. Every point $z\in Z_j$ mapping to $s_i$ has a corresponding point $t\in T_{i,a_i(j)}$ and an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{Z_j,z}\cong\mathcal O_{T_{i,a_i(j)},t}$. Over $U$ every intermediate scheme is isomorphic to $U$. If all prescribed centers are singular points, all global centers are singular points [def-weil-regular-scheme]. When $r=0$ or all $n_i=0$, the tower is the identity.

source.place: Tag 0BFY, resolve-lemma-equivalence-sequence-blowups, converse construction; section-modifications, equation-equivalence and lemma-equivalence-fibre (Tag 0BFX). The intermediate local-ring identifications are localization at the base, applied at every stage.

proof.text: Order the pairs $(i,k)$ with $1\leq i\leq r$ and $0\leq k<n_i$ lexicographically. This is a word of length $N=\sum_i n_i$. At stage $j$ let $a_i(j)$ count the letters with first coordinate $i$ already used. We construct by induction an integral normal Noetherian $Z_j\to S$, isomorphic to $U$ over $U$, and isomorphisms $Z_j\times_SS_i\cong T_{i,a_i(j)}$ over $S_i$, compatible with every preceding arrow. Initially $Z_0=S$, $a_i(0)=0$, and the isomorphisms are the identity base changes. If the word is empty this already gives the required identity tower.

source.place: Tag 0BFY, resolve-lemma-equivalence-sequence-blowups, converse: order the local blowups and initialize the induction

proof.text: Here is the localization calculation used at every stage, including the next stage before its normality is known. For any morphism $f:Z\to S$ put $Z_i=Z\times_SS_i$ with projection $p_i$. On an affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ containing $s_i$, write $s_i=\mathfrak p_i$ and $M=A\setminus\mathfrak p_i$. The canonical local-scheme morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}A_{\mathfrak p_i}\to V$. If $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset f^{-1}(V)$, its pullback has ring $B\otimes_AA_{\mathfrak p_i}=M^{-1}B$ by the cited localization-base-change statement. The localization-spectrum embedding identifies this chart with the primes $\mathfrak q\subset B$ avoiding the image of $M$. These chart identifications agree on restrictions because they are all induced by $p_i$. Thus $p_i$ identifies $|Z_i|$ with $f^{-1}(\operatorname{gen}(s_i))$ with its subspace topology. In particular the points over $s_i$ correspond bijectively, with their fibre subspace topologies.

source.place: Tag 01J6 and equation 02NA; Tag 01K1, schemes-lemma-fibre-topological, proof by affine localization; Algebra Tags 00DK and 00E3

proof.text: For a prime $\mathfrak q$ occurring in the preceding calculation, let $\mathfrak q'=M^{-1}\mathfrak q$. Every element of $M$ is already a unit in $B_{\mathfrak q}$. Consequently the maps $B_{\mathfrak q}\to(M^{-1}B)_{\mathfrak q'}$ and $(b/m)/(c/n)\mapsto bn/(mc)$ are inverse ring homomorphisms: the denominators $m,c$ avoid $\mathfrak q$, and checking their two composites on fractions gives the identity. Using the affine description of local rings gives $\mathcal O_{Z,p_i(t)}\cong\mathcal O_{Z_i,t}$, by the actual structural local homomorphism. In particular $p_i$ is flat: its stalk modules are the base local rings themselves, whose tensor functor is the identity. For every point of $Z$ over $s_i$ this proves precisely the local-ring identification required in the item.

source.place: Equation 02NA and the affine-local calculation in schemes-lemma-fibre-topological (Tag 01K1); repeated localization at the corresponding prime

proof.text: Suppose $j<N$ and the next letter is $(i,a_i(j))$. Let $t$ be the prescribed reduced closed center in $T_{i,a_i(j)}$. Through the induction isomorphism it is a point of $Z_j\times_SS_i$ over $s_i$, hence corresponds to a unique $z\in Z_j$ over $s_i$ by step 2. The point $t$ is closed in the local fibre, so $z$ is closed in the global fibre. This fibre is a closed subspace of $Z_j$, being the inverse image of the closed singleton $\{s_i\}$; therefore $z$ is closed in $Z_j$. Give $\{z\}$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure. The cited reduced-subscheme statement gives its quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_z$, equal on every affine chart containing $z$ to the maximal ideal of $z$, and equal to the unit ideal on charts missing $z$. By the induction hypothesis $Z_j$ has an affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, so it is locally Noetherian, and the ring $R$ of every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Z_j$ is Noetherian. Hence $\mathcal I_z(\operatorname{Spec}R)$, which is $R$ or the maximal ideal of $z$, is finitely generated by the definition of a Noetherian ring. Thus $\mathcal I_z$ is a quasi-coherent ideal whose restriction to every affine open is a finitely generated ideal; in particular it is of finite type.

source.place: Tag 0BFY, resolve-lemma-equivalence-sequence-blowups, center correspondence; Tag 0BFX, resolve-lemma-equivalence-fibre; Schemes Tag 01J3, schemes-lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme

proof.text: The center pulls back with its reduced structure, not just its support. For the active $i$, in the charts of step 2 containing $z$, let $\mathfrak q$ be its maximal ideal. Its pullback ideal is $M^{-1}\mathfrak q$ and the quotient is $M^{-1}(B/\mathfrak q)=B/\mathfrak q$, since $M\cap\mathfrak q=\varnothing$ and $B/\mathfrak q$ is a field. Thus it is exactly the reduced point corresponding to $t$, by uniqueness of the reduced induced structure. For $\ell\ne i$, the canonical map $S_\ell\to S$ has image the generalizations of $s_\ell$; it misses the distinct closed point $s_i$. Hence the inverse image of $z$ in $Z_j\times_SS_\ell$ is empty and the pulled-back ideal is the unit ideal. Explicitly, on any chart where the center is present, the maximal ideals of $s_i$ and $s_\ell$ in $A$ are distinct, so an element of the former outside the latter is zero in the point quotient and becomes invertible after localization at $s_\ell$. The localized quotient is therefore zero. These ideal equalities agree on affine overlaps.

source.place: divisors-lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up, inverse image of the center; resolve-lemma-equivalence-sequence-blowups, inactive local factors

proof.text: Define $Z_{j+1}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_z}(Z_j)$ by the global blowup construction. The projections $Z_j\times_SS_\ell\to Z_j$ are flat by step 3, so the flat-base-change comparison is an isomorphism. Together with step 5, it identifies the active base change with the prescribed blowup $T_{i,a_i(j)+1}\to T_{i,a_i(j)}$. On every other local factor the center is empty; the complement isomorphism identifies its blowup with that factor by its structure map. Compose these comparisons with the induction isomorphisms and the fibre-product associativity isomorphisms. Set $a_i(j+1)=a_i(j)+1$ and keep the other counts fixed. All comparison isomorphisms are over their old factors, so their squares with the new arrows commute; previous squares remain those of the induction hypothesis.

The ideal $\mathcal I_z$ is nonzero. Indeed, if it were zero, on every affine of the gluing construction its Rees algebra would have zero positive-degree part, since $0^n=0$ for $n>0$. Its Proj is empty: the standard opens at positive-degree elements are all empty (the only such element is zero) and they cover Proj. Thus the glued blowup $Z_{j+1}$ would be empty. But its active base change is $T_{i,a_i(j)+1}$ by step 6, which is nonempty by the assumed integrality of the prescribed stages. This is a contradiction. Now the cited integral-blowup theorem, applied to the integral $Z_j$ and its nonzero finite-type ideal $\mathcal I_z$, proves that $Z_{j+1}$ is integral.

source.place: Tag 02ND, divisors-lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme; divisors-lemma-blowing-up-affine and the defining Rees algebra for the zero-ideal edge case

proof.text: The arrow $Z_{j+1}\to Z_j$ is proper by the properness statement for a finite-type quasi-coherent blowup ideal. Proper includes finite type; since $Z_j$ is Noetherian, the finite-type-over-Noetherian statement makes $Z_{j+1}$ Noetherian. The blowup-complement statement gives an isomorphism away from $z$. In particular this arrow restricts to an isomorphism over $U$, and composing it with the already constructed isomorphism over $U$ preserves that induction condition.

source.place: divisors-lemma-blowing-up-projective and the complement clause; Morphisms Tag 01T6, morphisms-lemma-finite-type-noetherian

proof.text: To check normality of $Z_{j+1}$, a point mapping into $U$ has the same local ring as its image in the normal $S$, by the isomorphism over $U$. Any other point maps to some $s_\ell$ and, by steps 2 and 3 applied to $Z_{j+1}\to S$, its local ring is isomorphic to that of the corresponding point in $Z_{j+1}\times_SS_\ell\cong T_{\ell,a_\ell(j+1)}$. These prescribed stages are normal by hypothesis. In both cases the local ring is an integrally closed domain, so $Z_{j+1}$ is normal in exactly the sense in the statement. This completes the induction without assuming that an arbitrary ordinary blowup preserves normality.

source.place: resolve-lemma-equivalence-sequence-blowups, converse, supplemented by the base-localization local-ring calculation at each stage

proof.text: After all $N$ letters, $a_i(N)=n_i$ and every required local arrow has occurred in its original order; other letters gave precisely the inserted identity arrows. The induction supplies all intermediate integrality, normality, Noetherianity and the arrowwise properness and complement isomorphisms. Steps 2 and 3 supply the asserted point and local-ring correspondences at every intermediate stage. If the prescribed centers are singular, their local rings are not regular. At each chosen global center the local ring is isomorphic to the corresponding local center ring by step 3; regularity of a Noetherian local ring, and its failure, is invariant under ring isomorphism directly from the generator and Krull-dimension definition. Thus every global center is singular. The empty word covers both $r=0$ and the case when every $n_i=0$.

There are no new nodes and the statement is unchanged. All ten steps are correct. The lexicographic schedule and the induction invariants are stated explicitly (D4/D5). Steps 2–3 do the localization chart and local-ring calculation, with flatness. Step 5 pulls back the reduced center: the residue field on the active factor, the unit ideal on the inactive ones because a distinct closed point is not a generalization. Step 6 is the flat blowup comparison plus the complement theorem for the empty center. Step 7 excludes the zero ideal without circularity (S=Spec K is excluded by integrality of T) and only then applies 02ND. Steps 8–10 give properness, Noetherianity, pointwise normality and invariance of singularity. Tested: r=0, all n_i=0, a DVR point, lengths (2,1), a zero-dimensional base. One fault, repaired (C4/E1): step 4 proved finite generation of I_z only on a Noetherian affine cover, but the cited lem-per-integral-blowup-projective-geometry requires a finitely generated ideal on every affine open. The fix adds pqf-def-locnoeth and the Mathlib leaf pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth (every affine open of a locally Noetherian scheme is Noetherian) to step 4, rewrites its last sentences and recomputes proof_deps. The nagata blowup theorems cited are Lean-closed tools. There is no duplicate; the normalized-tower sibling is a different statement. No SGA is cited.
